feature: ArkWeb and direct system Browser public login-page comparison
precondition: No username, password, cookie value, screenshot, page text, URL text, or raw accessibility tree is read, stored, or emitted.

system_browser.action: Launch the device Browser through the standard view-data action and wait 12 seconds.
system_browser.generic_evidence: Two Navigation components, one Web component, Browser-chrome marker true, Cloudflare-resource marker true, verification-marker false.

nextn_arkweb.action: Install the current debug-signed NextN HAP with first-party periodic ArkWeb-session capture; navigate by the Settings Account row only; wait 15 seconds without entering account data.
nextn_arkweb.generic_evidence: One Navigation component, one Web component, Browser-chrome marker false, Cloudflare-resource marker true, verification-marker false, and no native loading indicator remained.

result: Passed: NextN opened a real ArkWeb login surface using its controller-attached UA and cookie configuration. Both containers loaded Cloudflare-related resources in the same bounded observation. The ArkWeb Cloudflare marker remained after 15 seconds, so this run explicitly does not assert Cloudflare completion or account authentication.
session_boundary: The system Browser and ArkWeb own separate cookie jars. NextN intentionally captures only trusted ArkWeb first-party session state; it cannot and must not import Browser cookies. The visible ArkWeb page now polls its URL-scoped cookie state while open so a same-page login completion is captured without DOM inspection, cookie logging, or credential access.
cleanup: Temporary host/device layout files are removed and NextN is restarted at its root route.
